record.original_question: Let A133058 be the sequence with a_0=a_1=1 and, for n≥2, a_n=a_{n-1}+n+1 when gcd(a_{n-1},n)=1 and a_n=a_{n-1}/gcd(a_{n-1},n) otherwise; then remove duplicate values to obtain A339571. Explain the combinatorial or arithmetic reason that the associated 4-regular graphs of this de-duplicated GCD sequence exhibit the striking structure shown in the paper.

evidence.quote: This sequence is derived from A133058: we consider A133058 and remove all duplicates resulting in the sequence A339571. A133058 (proposed by C. Zizka) has an iterative definition: a_0 = a_1 = 1 and, for n ≥ 2, a_n = a_{n-1} + n + 1 if gcd(a_{n-1}, n) = 1 and a_n = a_{n-1}/gcd(a_{n-1}, n) otherwise.
Several other examples are so mysterious (2.3, 2.6, 2.7, 2.10, 2.11) that it is difficult to say what one would expect.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define an integer sequence (a_n)_{n≥0} by a_0 = a_1 = 1 and, for n ≥ 2,
  a_n = a_{n-1} + n + 1   if gcd(a_{n-1}, n) = 1,
  a_n = a_{n-1} / gcd(a_{n-1}, n)   otherwise.
Let (b_k)_{k≥0} be the subsequence obtained by listing the values of (a_n) in order of first occurrence (that is, by removing every term equal to some earlier term).

For each integer N ≥ 1, build a 4-regular graph G_N as follows: the vertex set is {b_0, b_1, …, b_{N-1}}, and each vertex b_k is joined by an edge to its four nearest neighbors in the sequence, namely b_{k-2}, b_{k-1}, b_{k+1}, b_{k+2} (indices interpreted cyclically, multi-edges and loops suppressed).

When drawn using a force-directed layout, the graphs G_N display pronounced large-scale structure (clusters, branching patterns, and apparent self-similarity) rather than a generic random-looking 4-regular graph. Provide a combinatorial or arithmetic explanation for this observed structure: identify properties of the recurrence and of the de-duplication map n ↦ k(n) that account for the qualitative features of the graphs G_N.
artifact.status_search_result: The recurrence defining the underlying sequence is recorded as OEIS A133058 and its de-duplication as A339571, but no published combinatorial or arithmetic explanation for the striking graph structure has been located. The question appears to remain an unresolved empirical observation.
